lifespan.headline: You're likely to live to about 100. Most people like you live to between 89 and 110+.
lifespan.caveat: Proof of concept: a rough estimate, not a prediction for you. It repeats the survey model's one-year risk at each later age with your answers held fixed, so it can never be truly accurate. LifeTwin then focuses on your relative health score. The model was only checked up to age 79, so the ages past that are a rougher guess. The curve is followed only to age 110, so "110+" means at least 110.

current.interpretation: Estimated cumulative survival among similar survey profiles, not an individual death date or medical prognosis.

alternative.interpretation: Estimated cumulative survival among similar survey profiles, not an individual death date or medical prognosis.

result.interpretation: Difference between two model profiles, not the benefit of changing a habit.
warnings: BMI, sleep and sitting profile contrasts do not estimate intervention effects; the high-BMI fitted slope is near zero and slightly inverse.
A higher weight is never shown as a benefit: the model's BMI link is not evidence that gaining weight helps.

lifespan.headline: You're likely to live to about 83. Most people like you live to between 77 and 92.
lifespan.caveat: Proof of concept: a rough estimate, not a prediction for you. It extends the survey model's 5-year risk with the 2024 US life table, so it can never be truly accurate. LifeTwin then focuses on your relative health score. Your age is outside the ages the model was checked on (35–79), so this is even rougher.
